    <title>💌 Newsletter #008 - Of Age Gating (still), Claudia Delusions, and Getting Left Behind</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T13:27:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>technically-good</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;h1 id=in-this-edition&gt;✨ In This Edition ✨&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;📟 &lt;strong&gt;Short-Form Content:&lt;/strong&gt; Of &lt;em&gt;Claudia Delusions&lt;/em&gt;, "Tokenmaxxing", and goblins&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;📰 &lt;strong&gt;Long-Form Content:&lt;/strong&gt; Yes, we're still on Age Gating&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;🌞 &lt;strong&gt;Good News!&lt;/strong&gt;: Elected officials are warming up to the idea of alternative platforms; No, you won't get "left behind;" and more AI data centre bans are happening.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;📯 &lt;strong&gt;The Post-Script:&lt;/strong&gt; Terry Godier's &lt;a href='https://www.terrygodier.com/the-boring-internet/ascii' target='_blank'&gt;&lt;em&gt;The Boring Internet&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;h1 id=short-form-content&gt;📟 Short-Form Content&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h2 id=chatbots-ai&gt;Chatbots ("AI")&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;"You can't use an LLM in any context where &lt;strong&gt;being wrong is a problem&lt;/strong&gt;" is &lt;a href='https://fed.brid.gy/r/https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:wbtjiqd5pshd5tsvwjv6xmr3/post/3mke34nomvk24'&gt;a quote I came across on Mastodon&lt;/a&gt;, and as a data person who deeply cares about accuracy, data safety &amp; security, proper access rights and PII management and all that good stuff, this &lt;strong&gt;resonates deeply&lt;/strong&gt; with me.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;AI is excellent at moving fast and breaking things 🚀, like &lt;a href='https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/claude-powered-ai-coding-agent-deletes-entire-company-database-in-9-seconds-backups-zapped-after-cursor-tool-powered-by-anthropics-claude-goes-rogue'&gt;nuking your entire prod db in 9 seconds&lt;/a&gt; (including backups.) Remember, this is critical technology, and you'll be left behind if you don't let an LLM nuke your db into oblivion! Sometimes it even apologizes after, which is nice.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href='https://mastodon.social/@mattsheffield/116500991239336079'&gt;&lt;em&gt;The Claudia Delusion&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/a&gt; happened. I'm pretty sure all the jokes re: &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_God_Delusion' target='_blank'&gt;&lt;strong&gt;that book&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/a&gt; Dawkins wrote have already been made, so I'm just going to let this sit here on its own.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Remember how I'd been saying that the "AI" (LLM) bill was &lt;strong&gt;going to become due&lt;/strong&gt; really soon? So yeah, &lt;a href='https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/04/github-will-start-charging-copilot-users-based-on-their-actual-ai-usage/'&gt;that's starting to happen.&lt;/a&gt; Some folks are even getting &lt;a href='https://l3ib.org/@smn/116529758398137217'&gt;front-row seats&lt;/a&gt; to this! (Yay?) Non-tech teams &lt;a href='https://infosec.exchange/@stacksmashing/116528291966948969'&gt;shipping production vulns&lt;/a&gt; and leaking data to the public thru vibe-coding is going to get a whooooole lot more expensive.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If you're not "&lt;a href='https://pivot-to-ai.com/2026/04/28/tokenmaxxing-how-much-did-you-spend-in-tokens-ceo-of-tokens/'&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenmaxxing&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/a&gt;," are you even &lt;a href='https://i.kym-cdn.com/entries/icons/original/000/018/666/How_Do_You_Do_Fellow_Kids_meme_banner_image.jpg'&gt;with it&lt;/a&gt; anymore!? Anyways, I maintain that &lt;a href='https://techhub.social/@technically_good/116462402674044578'&gt;we should ask the CEO of peanut butter&lt;/a&gt; on recommendations on how much peanut butter we should all be eating every day.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;ChatGPT 5.5 just &lt;a href='https://techhub.social/@technically_good/116533137164431327'&gt;really likes to talk about goblins&lt;/a&gt;, ok!? It's not model collapse.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;h2 id=non-chatbots&gt;Non-Chatbots&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;We really need more differentiated media accounts of &lt;em&gt;phishing&lt;/em&gt; vs &lt;em&gt;hacks/breaches&lt;/em&gt;. No, Signal was not &lt;a href='https://ard.social/@tagesschau/116455165441679308'&gt;hacked&lt;/a&gt; (link in German). Some of its users fell for phishing, and &lt;a href='https://techhub.social/@technically_good/116455596733985546'&gt;even the most secure chat app on the planet can't protect from that&lt;/a&gt;. (And let's not even get started on that these are the same people that decide our digital futures via legislation...)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;h1 id=long-form-content&gt;📰 Long-Form Content&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h2 id=a-hrefhttpstechnically-goodcablog2026-04-age-gating-isnt-it-target_blankyes-were-still-on-age-gatinga&gt;&lt;a href='https://technically-good.ca/blog/2026-04-age-gating-isnt-it/' target='_blank'&gt;Yes, We're Still on Age-Gating&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Yes, we're back on &lt;strong&gt;age gating&lt;/strong&gt;, because a) &lt;a href='https://www.tomshardware.com/software/operating-systems/california-introduces-age-verification-law' target='_blank'&gt;more places&lt;/a&gt; &lt;a href='https://www.aol.com/news/missouri-lawmakers-consider-age-verification-214342830.html' target='_blank'&gt;are considering&lt;/a&gt; / intent on pushing this sort of thing through, and b) there's more and more evidence piling up that indicates this just &lt;a href='https://www.dexerto.com/entertainment/uk-kids-are-bypassing-age-verification-by-drawing-on-fake-mustaches-3360895/' target='_blank'&gt;isn't working&lt;/a&gt;. As people who are somewhat familiar with the subject all had predicted.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Oh, and c), because I haven't had time to finish my next long-form post, as a lot of Life ™️ has been happening, and I've had to make some changes and take a step back.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But enough about me! Coming back to age gating, it definitely &lt;a href='https://technically-good.ca/blog/2026-04-age-gating-isnt-it/' target='_blank'&gt;isn't all it's cracked up to be&lt;/a&gt;, because:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;it is a thinly-veiled &lt;strong&gt;surveillance information grab&lt;/strong&gt;. For folks claiming this is just like getting ID'd at the bar when you order your Molson's or whatever: &lt;a href='https://sfba.social/@minmi/116494534847016854' target='_blank'&gt;No, it's not.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;it's a &lt;strong&gt;digital sovereignty issue&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;online communities can be &lt;strong&gt;Good&lt;/strong&gt;, Actually&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;... it's probably &lt;strong&gt;not going to work&lt;/strong&gt; (we've gotten &lt;a href='https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/most-australian-teens-admit-social-111400429.html' target='_blank'&gt;even more data&lt;/a&gt; &lt;a href='https://fosstodon.org/@8tpercent/116483115227498657' target='_blank'&gt;on this &lt;/a&gt;since I published the article; and yes, &lt;a href='https://social.heise.de/@vowe/116515807603012363' target='_blank'&gt;fake moustaches&lt;/a&gt; are back in fashion)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;age gating means &lt;strong&gt;dancing around the real issue&lt;/strong&gt; of &lt;strong&gt;holding Big Tech accountable.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Read the full article &lt;a href='https://technically-good.ca/blog/2026-04-age-gating-isnt-it/' target='_blank'&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And lastly - especially if age gating is being suggested, proposed, or otherwise discussed in your area - &lt;em&gt;The time to speak up is now.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;h1 id=good-news&gt;🌞 Good News!&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href='https://mas.to/@carnage4life/116504559534707171' target='_blank'&gt;A Chinese court has ruled that companies cannot legally fire workers and replace them with AI.&lt;/a&gt; See also &lt;a href='https://toot.cafe/@baldur/116516986307530768' target='_blank'&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Signal is working on a &lt;a href='https://mastodon.social/@knoppix95/116512044363013083' target='_blank'&gt;standalone desktop app&lt;/a&gt;!&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href='https://mastodon.social/@dansup/116516756836881122'&gt;Elected officials&lt;/a&gt; are very much warming up to the idea of the fediverse / &lt;a href='https://eupolicy.social/@hpod16/116538344713848285' target='_blank'&gt;app alternatives&lt;/a&gt; to the US-American, Big Tech corporations.&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;See also, a number of major parties in Germany &lt;a href='https://cybernews.com/tech/erman-politicians-x/' target='_blank'&gt;all left twitter&lt;/a&gt; last week.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A &lt;em&gt;lot&lt;/em&gt; of places are now &lt;a href='https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/ai-data-center-bans-are-rapidly-multiplying-across-the-us-69-jurisdictions-block-new-builds-with-four-moves-noted-as-permanent' target='_blank'&gt;banning AI data centres&lt;/a&gt; from their cities, doorsteps, and open fields. I am on board with this kind of NIMBY-ism.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;France and Germany have unveiled &lt;a href='https://www.techspot.com/news/107225-france-germany-unveil-docs-collaborative-tool-rival-us.html'&gt;"Docs,"&lt;/a&gt; a European collaborative writing platform that can serve as a digitally sovereign alternative to Google Docs, Notion, etc.&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;While we're here, let's talk about &lt;a href='https://github.com/suitenumerique/docs/blob/main/docs/assets/europe_opensource.png'&gt;their logo&lt;/a&gt;, which involves the cutest baguette, cheese, and Brezel (yep) trio I've ever seen. We all need a little bit of whimsy in our lives.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;No, you won't in fact be "left behind" if you don't use AI. I really like &lt;a href='https://heychat.bearblog.dev/you-wont-be-left-behind-if-you-dont-use-ai/'&gt;this nuanced article on the Chatscape blog&lt;/a&gt; that likens the current AI boosterism to the "smart home" craze of the 2010s. Here's a small quote, but I would encourage you to read the whole article:&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;"A decade ago, tech enthusiasts predicted that every home would be a fully automated hub of &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_of_things'&gt;Internet of Things (IoT)&lt;/a&gt; devices, and those who didn't adapt would live in "dumb," inefficient homes. Today, our dumb houses are functioning perfectly well."&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There's &lt;a href='https://beige.party/@bimmer/116459704122637258' target='_blank'&gt;memes&lt;/a&gt; about this too.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;h1 id=the-post-script&gt;📯 The Post-Script&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h2 id=following-reading&gt;Following &amp; Reading&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;This excellent article on &lt;a href='https://www.terrygodier.com/the-boring-internet/ascii'&gt;&lt;em&gt;The Boring Internet&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/a&gt; by Terry Godier. Great explanations of the differences between platforms and protocols, and "fossils" from like 1982 that are "still load-bearing."&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://nostalgia.bearblog.dev/parental-love/</id>
    <title>客观地评估父母之爱或许可以救命</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T06:20:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>nostalgia</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;这篇文章受到博文&lt;a href='https://blog.solazy.me/20260508/'&gt;《别让爱只剩下「早知道」》&lt;/a&gt;的启发，原文很好，我只想补充一个角度。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;隔离期是一段精神疾病大爆发的时期，人们很多以前能压制住的东西可能压制不住了。我在COVID前后接触到了几个抑郁症病人，并曾经和他们很亲近。他们中的两位已经死了，有几位还活着，还有位不确定是否还活着。这些自杀和关于自杀的探讨在我二十岁末留下了长长的，黑暗的阴影。他们中男女，东西方，本地人和移民都有。虽然他们中的每个人都给我带来了或多或少的痛苦，尤其是离世的那两位。但他们都是很棒的年轻人，我一点也不后悔结交并且倾听他们的想法。他们中的每个人，都曾遭受过父母的忽视或虐待。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;他们全都很聪明，没有任何一位&lt;em&gt;真正地&lt;/em&gt;依赖父母。以他们的工作能力经济上支持自己绰绰有余，但这并不妨碍他们父母几乎给他们中的每个人都留下了重大而且持久的心理创伤。其中一位已故的朋友在自杀之前，已经从印度远渡重洋生活在欧洲，也无法摆脱他的家人亲自上门骚扰。我在他过世以后和他的家人通电话。他的家人似乎仍然并不觉得在我以西方视角看来明显是跟踪（stalking）的骚扰行为有什么错。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;我虽然没有得过抑郁症或者自杀的念头，但是通过这些朋友的经历那里我学到很多东西。最重要的一课是：虽然没有人能改变过去和过去带来的创伤，这些都需要在专业人士的指导下进行疗愈。但成年人对父母造成的负面影响可以执行一定的隔离（containment）。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;p&gt;在美国，主流观点认为父母和成年孩子关系平等。我看见有美国人讲："我对待我成年的孩子就像我对待其他成年人。对其他成年朋友不当讲的话，我对我的孩子也会闭嘴。"这种态度在日常交往中是肉眼可见的，因为往往边界感强，遏制住控制欲的父母，才有机会留在成年孩子的生活中。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;但很多移民父母拒绝接受本地文化。比如上文提到的跟踪行为，我自己的父母也曾在美国想要骚扰我，以我威胁报警告终。有个同事已经断联的母亲威胁去她办公室大闹，她不得不匿名询问怎么办。同事们都劝她告知公司保安，这样如果母亲真的出现就可以实施拦截。我想象了一下成年员工的父母跑去世界著名互联网公司总部撒泼的画面，不厚道地感觉有些喜感。这招实在太亚洲了，西方父母会害怕被警察逮捕，一般不干。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;相比之下我的朋友让我觉得非常可惜。他家人会在社交媒体上搭讪他的朋友或在欧洲实体跟踪。如果我的朋友象那个同事一样和欧洲本地人一起商量对策，那么或许他还能用当地法律给自己打造边界，隐私，甚至一条生路。死亡这件事没有如果。他的经历让我学到重要的一课：Shut that shit down early.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;父母会得寸进尺是因为这的确就是场战争：一场成年人保卫生活主权的战争。有些亚洲父母，比如我自己的，正面打不过也许还会没完没了地来迂回游击战，因为这些父母本质上不愿意接受“成年人享有对自己生活的绝对主权”，这是他们的心理问题，需要他们自己去处理。但是如果旷日持久地拖下去，即使有幸不危害心理健康也会浪费大量时间精力，限制年轻人其他方面的发展。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;p&gt;物理分割只是第一步。我那些还在世的朋友中，受到主要的精神折磨来自现实和叙事的不一致。在我看来，这种叙事是造成很多心理问题的根源。而且这个叙事无论是在东方还是在西方，都是广泛存在的，那就是：父母爱孩子。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;重要的是，这只是“叙事”（narrative），甚至说是政治宣传（Propaganda）也不为过。它在所有人类社会传播如此之广，意味着维持这个叙事对每个社会的当权者，或者说有机会发出声音的人，都有极大的好处。在中国社会，它似乎被提升到了公理的程度，就像派值，或是一党专制。所有人都自动接受，不容置疑，没有人会在公共舆论场上挑战它。而在英语世界，因为言论自由，这条“公理”在互联网上就像基督教一样，正在逐年被削弱瓦解。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Reddit父母皆祸害大组r/RaisedByNarcissists订阅量趋势：&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/nostalgia/image-14.webp" alt="image" /&gt;
&lt;img src="https://bear-images.sfo2.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/nostalgia/image-15.webp" alt="image" /&gt;
数据截止至2023年八月，现订阅量一百一十万。（数据来源：&lt;a href='https://subredditstats.com/r/raisedbynarcissists'&gt;Subreddit Stats&lt;/a&gt;）&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;无论在中西方，我想每人仔细想都能举出一大堆父母不爱孩子的例子，中国人大量弃养女婴首当其冲。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;既然有这条“公理”存在，孩子就会对父母有期待。但由于它的实质是政治宣传而没有什么事实依据，由此“公理”做出的推论由于逻辑不通或者和现实起冲突会导致大量的认知失调（Cognitive dissonance）。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;认知失调具体看上去是怎样的呢？我曾经有个巴基斯坦裔朋友，她三个兄弟姐妹自从上了大学，就跟家里断联了，她父母很有钱，但是父亲爱打孩子。她跟我说打孩子不属于虐待（abuse）。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;我问：假设你丈夫如果打你，算不算虐待？&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;她说：算。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;我问：那你父亲打你们这帮孩子，算不算虐待？&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;她：算，不对，父母打孩子不一样，而且虐待这个词有法律意义，全世界各地很多文化里父母都打孩子，我们不应该把这件事上升到虐待这么严重的程度。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;我：你如果不能接受你丈夫打你，我相信如果他打你你会马上离开。那么为什么你认为你兄弟姐妹应该接受你爸打他们？&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;后来我们就不再是朋友了。¯(ツ)/¯&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;一旦打上“父母爱孩子”这个思乡钢印，认知失调会渗入一个人的方方面面。放在同辈间明显是虐待的行为，在中国被美化成打是亲骂是爱。我想这是为什么在中国所谓“虐恋”文学这么流行的原因，连美国腐女都注意到了中国耽美文学里描述的关系有多不健康。我想虐恋文学也许是中国年轻人处理思想钢印所带来的逻辑不自洽，继而需要对各种虐待行为合理化而对应（cope）的表现之一。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;如果一个人对生活中的一项关系质量接受标准低到尘埃，她就无法自洽地将健康的标准运用到其他关系中。我观察美国黄热病喜欢亚女的原因之一可能是，黄热病敏锐地捕捉到了很多亚女对所有关系质量的要求偏低。这可能是普遍的低亲子关系质量带来的：既然一个人的生活各方面都能被父母亲戚随便插嘴插手，那反映出这个人边界感虚弱。一个没有边界感的人非常适合其他控制狂乘虚而入施以控制。中西部信仰基督教的女性有非常类似的困扰。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;边界感的缺失在人年轻的时候不容易被高等教育和高收入快速治愈。西方心理学认为，人只能在安全健康的关系中得到治愈，哪怕这种关系只有一个。心理咨询师起到的作用是或许成为那第一个健康关系。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;也就是说，被父母虐待过的成年人与家庭以外的人更容易形成不健康关系，恶性循环。其中极端者最终会感到四面楚歌，被逼入绝境。这是我认为人应该将“父母爱孩子”从公理降级为观察结果的原因。因为如果用这条“公理”错误地解释自己的父母，可能会由于认知失调污染与整个世界的关系。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;p&gt;不可否认，这个世界上爱孩子的父母也是有很多的，在一些制度良好的社会甚至占大多数。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;那么如何客观判断父母是否爱自己呢？我想一定距离是必要的，父母的叙事在成长过程中无法回避会对孩子产生巨大影响。必须从家人的影响中走出去，与其他的人尝试塑造更健康的关系。这些关系一是产生对比，二作为是精神独立的支点。我与父母的关系很不健康，但我幸运在可以依赖家庭以外的关系，这些朋友在最低点会拉我一把，帮我抵挡住抑郁症。不像我父母比较喜欢落井下石。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;然后可以问自己，我父母对我做过的这些行为，说过的话，我会对我真正爱的人做吗？&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;爱的人可以是伴侣，是朋友，是自己现实或者想象中的孩子。只要觉得自己爱得真心实意就行。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;任何议题证实比较难，证伪是容易的，如果答案是“绝对不会”。那么对“父母是否爱自己”这个问题也可以猜得八九不离十了，人就算扭成麻花也不可能证实已经证伪的命题。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;如果人没干罪大恶极比如杀人放火的事情，父母不爱自己的孩子或者使用孩子达成某些目标的工具，100%是父母的错。父母选择将孩子降生到这个世界，父母强制孩子进入不对等亲子关系和施予乱七八糟的期望。被动降生的孩子无权说不。遇到不爱或者没有爱人能力的父母纯粹是运气不好。就像路上不小心被鸟拉屎拉头上了，天灾人祸，难道还能跟鸟较劲不成？但可以选择以后不把车停在鸟树下。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;未成年人意识到父母不爱自己更麻烦一些，因为没有自由。美国人给出的标准建议是：养精蓄锐，好好读书，争取拿奖学金读大学，早日经济独立，独立以后马上跑。跟移民一个路数，我们这个移民国家，“打不过就跑”是民族精神。&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;死亡以外的出路还是很多的。社会灌输的所谓公理不必接受，毕竟过去所有重大科学和社会变革都是以前的“公理”被推翻的过程：相对论，地球绕着太阳转，男女平等，政府的合法性来自民选，等等。破除原有“公理”的过程对个人来说必然痛苦，没法绕过，就像美国人走出基督教经常搞得死去活来的。但至少可以知道，这个世界上正有很多青少年和年轻人正遭受着类似的痛苦，绝大多数人还是活着走出来了，无需因为父母的错惩罚自己。&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://nostalgia.bearblog.dev/parental-love/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-09T06:20:00+00:00</published>

    <id>https://skuka.online/when-someone-upvotes-my-post-it-feels-like-a-friendly-smile-by-a-stranger/</id>
    <title>when someone upvotes my post, it feels like a friendly smile by a stranger</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T11:15:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>skuka</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;i feel the sense of community here on bearblog. i was thinking of why that is, and one of the reasons is that sometimes, people upvote my posts. it is not really an interaction in the traditional sense, instead, it feels like a friendly presence of a stranger. i know nothing about them, but i know that they feel something that makes them upvote a post - that might be agreement, or maybe they like my page design, or maybe they are just thinking "why not". what i am getting from it, though, is a friendly vibe - a stranger is friendly to me!
it feels nice.
i upvote all the posts that i read to the end for the same reason - it's fun to be a friendly presence. like a lil friendly ghost almost.&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://blog.sulimans.space/dumbphone/</id>
    <title>the dumbphone idea is nothing but an idea</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T19:48:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>suliman</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;A few days ago, I watched a retro buyers’ guide for iPods. I was considering an iPod Nano 7 as an offline music player with Bluetooth capabilities with no internet access. Only problem is, these devices are old, can only be purchased secondhand and are hard to repair. So if the battery hadn’t been charged in a while and I charge it, it might inflate and burst through the fragile screen. The only advantage an iPod like that carries over my Apple Watch is that it’s easier to flash my music library to from my Mac instead of relying on Bluetooth transfer from my iPhone. So, when I sensed the futility in wasting time on these retro guides and devices, I went to the &lt;a href='https://www.sidephone.com/'&gt;Sidephone&lt;/a&gt; page, which sported a sundial like the iPod Classic, to check its price again and whether it shipped to my country of residence.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I was starry-eyed at the sundial that it comes with because that phone could be a more sophisticated music player and probably a main daily driver. My sister walked in on me, saw what I was looking it, and then asked me why consider such a limited phone. I explained my reasons, then she asked me what apps that phone had. Through the course of the conversation, we got to a point where I was giving her a „what’s on my phone?“ tour through the limited set of apps on my current phone. When I got to the banking, government ID, social security, public transport, password management, and MFA apps, she promptly asked me: „Well, can that phone run those apps?“ And I said, no, it probably can’t. And probably never will.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then it dawned on me anew that the thought of going dumbphone, or semi-dumbphone in the case of the Sidephone, was nothing but a thought. It will never be realized as long as I don’t plan on making my choice other people’s problem. My friend Pirate, who had been using a dumbphone for a few months, discussed the outsourcing nature of that decision in one of his recent posts „&lt;a href='https://blog.absurdpirate.com/to-smartphone-or-not-to-smartphone/'&gt;To Smartphone or Not to Smartphone&lt;/a&gt;“. This is further corroborated by Ava’s wife’s experience never using smartphones in „&lt;a href='https://blog.avas.space/dumbphone-wife/'&gt;my wife and her dumbphone&lt;/a&gt;,“ where she wrote: „Despite all Requests never to drop off something [in DHL’s package lockers] occasionally Deliveries still end up there and Ava has to handle that for me every Time.“&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Over a year ago and after she posted „&lt;a href='https://blog.avas.space/dumbphone/'&gt;dumbphones as a new status symbol&lt;/a&gt;“, me and Ava emailed about all the ways in which we are so dependent on some apps on smartphones that hinder our move to dumbphones. If I ever went dumbphone, it would mean I don’t need the above apps (banking, government ID, social security, public transport, password management, and MFA) which would mean someone else does the banking for me, I never need to ID myself online, because again, someone else does it for me or an analog, less convenient alternative exists, and I don’t use public transport because I have a car.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;All this is a privilege (the car’s a downgrade, though) that makes dumbphones a clear status symbol in my eyes. It says that you can fly through this world without all the mandatory software that life under this system makes necessary. Going dumbphone is thus so easy enough to attain as to make them within sight, yet always out of reach for any ordinary person.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And in any case, going dumbphone would only address the problem for me, one that not only affects me. This would be yet another instance of individualizing solutions to collective problems; problems that could be more effectively and conveniently addressed for us all instead of each of us unnecessarily chasing a solutions of our own.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;So I guess I’ll always keep looking at the other side and toying with the idea of pulling the trigger yet knowing full well that I realistically can’t.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://blog.sulimans.space/dumbphone/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-08T19:48:00+00:00</published>

  <entry>
    <id>https://sameoldstory.co/ive-been-blocking-social-media-on-the-weekends/</id>
    <title>I've been blocking social media on the weekends.</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T00:30:52.680065+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>sameoldstory</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I've started using &lt;a href='https://www.foqos.app/'&gt;Foqos&lt;/a&gt; to block social media on the weekends and it's been really nice!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It's good to try and keep my screentime down and when you're messing around on your phone there's usually something better you could be doing with your time, but in the end there's only a few apps that are actually bad habits for me and that's what I chose to block: Reddit and Bluesky. I don't need to block Instagram or Discord because for me those are just not applications I find myself spending much more than utilitarian time on (receiving and responding to messages, largely from people I know in real life).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Some phone fiddling, like responding to games on Chess.com or messing with my blog here, actually leaves me feeling good so I don't see any need to restrict it so long as I'm not using it to avoid my obligations or ignore my family or whatever.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It's been nice, though! It hasn't really made a difference in how much I go out and do things, having kids does enough of that and I have several social and club obligations on top of that. But the temptation to argue with people over the Internet when I'm tired or stressed out or bored is too much for me, and I can't honestly see myself giving up on it altogether but I think it can be nice (for me and everyone else in my life) to take a forced vacation from it fairly regularly.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;--&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;This post was last edited &lt;strong&gt;19 hours, 30 minutes ago&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://notesonliving.bearblog.dev/the-case-for-hope/</id>
    <title>The Case for Hope</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T17:55:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>notesonliving</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I am writing this for the times it feels like the only possible collective future is one where things inevitably get a lot worse.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;We live in the age of one-in-a-lifetime crises &lt;em&gt;occurring&lt;/em&gt;&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-1"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-1"&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; every few months, when a handful of tyrants deciding to start wars, bomb schools, blockade trade routes affect grain prices in the global south and fuel prices across the world, and your ability to pay for flight tickets to go see your family.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Every time you open your phone feeds you enter a battle against the colonization of your attention. There is an information war being beamed straight to your &lt;a href='https://seriousendeavor.com/i-need-to-check-the-device/' target='_blank'&gt;rectangle of hell&lt;/a&gt; making you second-guess everything you watch, hear or read, and what feels genuine is telling you to worry for your lives and your livelihood, because AI is coming for our jobs, fascism is back in fashion, and the next election cycle in your country might be the last you get to have. But perhaps you might like to entertain yourself by watching the richest people on the planet play dress-up for a gala funded by &lt;del&gt;a billionaire&lt;/del&gt; &lt;a href='https://cued.uic.edu/pain-points/' target='_blank'&gt;the man responsible for slave-like labor, below-living-wages&lt;/a&gt; and stifling &lt;a href='https://www.theguardian.com/media/2025/feb/26/jeff-bezos-washington-post-opinion' target='_blank'&gt;freedom of press&lt;/a&gt;?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Because you are reading this on the small web, you probably already know this. Chances are, you wouldn't be here if you weren't, in some measure, sick of it all, and craving a different experience of the world.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There is much to be said - and smarter people than I have been begging us to pay attention - about why it has come to this &lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-2"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-2"&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But today, I am not looking for sociopolitical analysis. I am looking for hope.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I am writing this mostly as a note to myself, but also because it is worth remembering again and again, especially when our power feels nonexistent and the relentlessness of crises eggs us on to give up, give in to cynicism, and accept the way things are, that it does not have to be this way.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I urge you (I urge myself):&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;consider this.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;We live in capitalism. Its power seems inescapable. So did the divine right of kings. Any human power can be resisted and changed by human beings. Resistance and change often begin in art, and very often in our art, the art of words. ― Ursula K. Le Guin&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And this.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Our strategy should be not only to confront empire, but to lay siege to it. To deprive it of oxygen. To shame it. To mock it. With our art, our music, our literature, our stubbornness, our joy, our brilliance, our sheer relentlessness – and our ability to tell our own stories. Stories that are different from the ones we’re being brainwashed to believe.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The corporate revolution will collapse if we refuse to buy what they are selling – their ideas, their version of history, their wars, their weapons, their notion of inevitability.
Remember this: We be many and they be few. They need us more than we need them.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Another world is not only possible, she is on her way. On a quiet day, I can hear her breathing. ― Arundhati Roy&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;We stand on the shoulders of our foremothers, who overcame many an injustice to make this world a better place for us, and have much to teach us.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I was going to die, sooner or later, whether or not I had even spoken myself. My silences had not protected me. Your silences will not protect you.... What are the words you do not yet have? What are the tyrannies you swallow day by day and attempt to make your own, until you will sicken and die of them, still in silence? We have been socialized to respect fear more than our own need for language. ― Audre Lorde&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;In which parts of my life do I feel closest to truth? When do I feel furthest away from it?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The distance between what is said today and what is known to be true has become an abyss. Of all the things at risk, the loss of an objective reality is perhaps the most dangerous. (...) When truth leaves us, when we let it slip away, when it is ripped from our hands, we become vulnerable to the appetite of whatever monster screams the loudest. ― Mon Mothma&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The System, the Empire, the Machine, the Capital, is counting on you to depoliticize, to look away, to get used to things. You shouldn't.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;To love. To be loved. To never forget your own insignificance. To never get used to the unspeakable violence and the vulgar disparity of life around you. To seek joy in the saddest places. To pursue beauty to its lair. To never simplify what is complicated or complicate what is simple. To respect strength, never power. Above all, to watch. To try and understand. To never look away. And never, never to forget. ― Arundhati Roy&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And finally, hope and choices are the most powerful tools at our disposal. Use them well, use them often.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;To be hopeful in bad times is not just foolishly romantic. It is based on the fact that human history is a history not only of cruelty, but also of compassion, sacrifice, courage, kindness. What we choose to emphasize in this complex history will determine our lives. If we see only the worst, it destroys our capacity to do something. (...) And if we do act, in however small a way, we don’t have to wait for some grand utopian future. The future is an infinite succession of presents, and to live now as we think human beings should live, in defiance of all that is bad around us, is itself a marvelous victory. ― Howard Zinn&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;hr&gt;
&lt;a href="https://notbyai.fyi" target="_blank" rel="noopener"&gt;
  &lt;img src="https://notbyai.fyi/img/written-by-human-not-by-ai-white.svg" alt="Written by Human, Not by AI"&gt;
&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;section class="footnotes"&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-1"&gt;&lt;p&gt;I emphasize &lt;em&gt;occurring&lt;/em&gt; because crises are not naturally occurring phenomena sent to us by god but very much a feature of &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis_theory' target='_blank'&gt;our current economic model.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;a href="#fnref-1" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-2"&gt;&lt;p&gt;Our friend Karl &lt;a href='https://qz.com/1269525/capitalism-is-unfolding-exactly-as-karl-marx-predicted' target='_blank'&gt;predicted quite a few things&lt;/a&gt; that have come to pass.&lt;a href="#fnref-2" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://notesonliving.bearblog.dev/the-case-for-hope/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-08T17:55:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://manateeswake.bearblog.dev/autism-humanities/</id>
    <title>STEM is not "more autistic" than the humanities</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T18:16:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>manateeswake</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;There's an autism stereotype that just won't die, and it never stops bugging me. It's the idea that the "default" autistic person is a STEM person, while an autistic person in the arts or humanities is atypical, an anomaly.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The "STEM autistic, arts neurotypical" dichotomy isn't as entrenched as it was a decade or two ago (and boy do I remember how entrenched it was), but I still see it floating around.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I see it in social media posts that claim a knack for fantasy and role-play sets PDA apart from Regular Old Autism. (That's a whole other can of worms that I don't want to try to talk about.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I see it in research studies like the one Autism Answers Back critiqued &lt;a href='https://autismanswersback.bearblog.dev/creativity-is-autistic-not-a-side-effect-or-misdiagnosis/'&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;. This study used closed-ended surveys and a time-limited task to measure creativity, yet didn't ask any open-ended questions that could've allowed participants to describe their creative process, or what creativity means for them. The study then drew the conclusion that autistic people don't show exceptional creativity unless we also have ADHD; that to be creative, we need some sort of add-on to offset our Regular Old Autism.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Recently I saw it in a social media post by an autistic creator whose work I respect. The post, a deep dive into differences between autistic and neurotypical communication, had a lot of care and thought put into it. But one small piece of it made me pause. "Artistic nuance" was listed as an inherent strength of neurotypical communication, while "STEM communication" was listed as a natural strength of autistic people. The post came with the caveat that these are generalizations, but calling artistic nuance neurotypical still didn't sit right with me. (And that's not even getting into the fact that neurodivergences besides autism exist.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I commented. I wasn't as nice as I should've been, and I feel bad about that, and I ended up deleting it later. But her reply ("I'm simply pointing out that we lean in different directions") reminded me of the excuse my former (thank goodness) therapist made after telling me women's brains were inherently worse at math.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The thing is, saying "X people are naturally good at Y subject, while A people are naturally good at B subject" isn't harmless. It's often used to pigeonhole human beings in racist, sexist, or ableist ways.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I'm not saying that autistic people in STEM aren't common, or that they're embodying a stereotype. Autistic people in STEM are great and deserve to be recognized.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I'm saying (or at least trying to say) that science or math shouldn't be considered more "typical" autistic strengths than the arts or humanities. Autistic artists or writers deserve better than the idea that their interests and talents make them closer to neurotypical than autistic engineers are.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And while we're at it, can we leave the humanities-vs-STEM binary in the past too? They can intermingle in amazing ways. When you see them as polar opposites, you miss that.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://manateeswake.bearblog.dev/autism-humanities/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-08T18:16:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://migrainebrain.bearblog.dev/a-rant-about-tv-shows/</id>
    <title>A rant about TV shows</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T13:19:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>migrainebrain</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I grew up watching TV in the 90s, which means I grew up watching TV series with 20+ episodes per season, released weekly, and that ran for years and years. Too many episodes, for too long, really. Beverly Hills 90210 had 10 seasons and some of them had more than 30 episodes! That's insane.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;But you know, for a while, around the 2010s, we had the perfect balance. The Americans, Breaking Bad, Mad Man... those were great quality TV shows that ran for 6, 7 seasons, released consistently every year, and that had around 13 weekly episodes per season. It was perfect: 13 quality episodes every year and a proper ending.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;And then, we ruined it all. It was fun for a while, having all these series with the whole season released all at once, binge-watching them for two days and moving on to the next one. But now it sucks. Quality wise, yes, we still have some great shows, of course. But they have like 7, 8 episodes per season, released all at once, we watch everything over a weekend and then we have to wait for like two, three years to watch the next season? And even when the episodes are released weekly, waiting for years for the next season is just ridiculous. And that's even being optimistic, since lately most shows get canceled after two seasons. I'm sick of it and I don't get it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;in 2023 I started watching The Great Door Prize (apple), and I was really into it. The show was renewed for a second season before the first season was released, and then it was canceled before the second season was released. What's up with that?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Also, there's the social aspect of it, which is mostly lost. We don't watch the same things at the same time anymore, so there's barely any conversation about it. I miss that. Remember how it was watching Lost? Waiting every week for a new episode, talking about it the next day, making stupid theories, arguing about the finale... Those were good days.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;div class="reply-email"&gt;
  &lt;a href="mailto:migrainebrain@pm.me?subject=Re:%20A rant about TV shows"&gt;Reply to this post.&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
or don't.
&lt;hr /&gt;

</content>
    <link href="https://migrainebrain.bearblog.dev/a-rant-about-tv-shows/" rel="alternate"/>

  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://cherrysroom.bearblog.dev/sodas-of-yore-strange-drinkables-from-new-york-in-1915-new/</id>
    <title>sodas of yore: strange drinkables from new york in 1915</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T07:12:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>cherrysroom</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;weather:&lt;/strong&gt; ☀️ goodbye clouds &lt;br /&gt;
&lt;strong&gt;critters:&lt;/strong&gt; my cat (i stayed inside all day)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;p&gt;today i flipped through &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href='https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Dispenser_s_Formulary_Or_Soda_Water/bFU2AQAAMAAJ'&gt;the dispenser's formulary&lt;/a&gt;,&lt;/em&gt; an american tome of recipes and knuckle-swatting advice for an aspiring soda jerk.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=notes&gt;notes&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;the authors want to be &lt;em&gt;absolutely clear&lt;/em&gt; with you that bad hygiene and slovenly habits and cheaping out on ingredients are unforgivable at the soda fountain. i've noticed that how-to manuals from this period can be pretty bossy, but maybe we need some of that when it comes to health hazards.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;some of the "luncheonette" offerings (p196) would go fantastically on &lt;a href='https://cherrysroom.bearblog.dev/low-effort-sandwiches/'&gt;my low-effort sandwiches page&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;there is a brief discussion and a couple of recipes on p86 for what they call "kumyss." i was like, gee, i've never heard of that, must be another extinct drink type. then i read "prepared by the tartars from the milk of mares" and realized i totally &lt;em&gt;had&lt;/em&gt; heard of it--i just knew it by the mongolian name &lt;em&gt;airag.&lt;/em&gt; i would never have imagined seeing airag in this context, but it seems it was popular back then. (the book's recipes use cow's milk, of course.)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;speaking of subverted expectations, there's a lot less apple than i thought i'd see, and a lot more pineapple, and &lt;em&gt;way&lt;/em&gt; more grape--as juice and as wine. we have really denormalized day-drinking outside of brunch. that said, most of the fruity soda recipes are variations on familiar themes of cherries and berries and citruses that would seem pretty normal today.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;h2 id=quotes&gt;quotes&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;In former years it was the general custom to use nothing but essences and extracts for soda beverages, but during the last ten years a change has taken place and nearly all first-class dispensers are using pure fruit syrups and so-called crushed or liquid fruits." (p34)&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;It has been well said that "drinks may come and drinks may go but the orange phosphate goes on forever." (p61)&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;"Use coloring matter sparingly and eschew the old fashioned 'foams.' Brilliant, frothy sodas are suspiciously unpopular these days." (p30)&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;"Remember that syrup making is not a boy's job—it is a fine art." (p30)&lt;/blockquote&gt;
&lt;h2 id=some-adorable-names&gt;some adorable names&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"fairies' wish"&lt;/strong&gt; (p37), a soda syrup of cream, vanilla, and strawberry.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"sea-side shake"&lt;/strong&gt; (p81), a shake like a grape-orange julius.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"may queen fizzette"&lt;/strong&gt; (p40), a soda syrup of blood orange, raspberry, wine, rose, and pineapple. the &lt;strong&gt;"palm beach queen"&lt;/strong&gt; (p44) is similar, but with grape juice instead of wine.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"razzle-dazzle"&lt;/strong&gt; (p61), a pineapple-ade with a little raspberry vinegar, which i believe here indicates the same thing as raspberry shrub. max miller made a &lt;a href='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3AWqxSnArKk&amp;pp=ygUPcmFzcGJlcnJ5IHNocnVi0gcJCQMLAYcqIYzv'&gt;nice video&lt;/a&gt; about it a while back. raspberry shrub is also called "raspberry sharp" in the book (p46), and there is a recipe for a peach shrub on p42.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=some-inexplicable-drink-names&gt;some inexplicable drink names&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"silurian"&lt;/strong&gt; (p47), a phosphate syrup of rosewater and pineapple juice. my head went straight to &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silurian'&gt;the silurian period&lt;/a&gt;, but it could be named for the &lt;a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silures'&gt;actual tribe&lt;/a&gt;. maybe the celts were pineapple farmers.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-1"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-1"&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"japanese thirst killer"&lt;/strong&gt; (p63), an orgeat phosphate with angostura bitters. don't just quench your thirst! kill it dead! i can't say what makes this flavor profile specifically japanese. a lot of the recipes called "japanese" here involve almond generally. i wonder why?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"crown prince fizz"&lt;/strong&gt; (p53), a strawberry-citrus soda that sounds like a rainbow brite character. was it named after edward VIII? i guess my countrymen have been obsessed with the british monarchy for a lot longer than i thought.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-2"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-2"&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"quaker freeze"&lt;/strong&gt; (p55), a raspberry-grape-orange slushie. 'religious society of friends freeze' must not have rolled off the tongue.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=syrup-burbank-special-p36&gt;syrup: "burbank special" (p36)&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;Plum extract ......... 2 drams&lt;br/&gt;
Quince extract ........ 2 drams&lt;br/&gt;
Fruit acid ........... 4 drams&lt;br/&gt;
Pineapple juice ...... 10 ounces&lt;br/&gt;
Simple syrup ......... 1 gallon
&lt;p&gt;Mix well. Serve as a phosphate.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;"fruit acid" refers to a 1:1 solution of citric acid in water or alcohol (p24).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;the syrup may be named after luther burbank, a horticulturalist responsible for many fruit and vegetable cultivars, among them several plums and quinces (and a beautiful white blackberry cultivar).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;i think we're missing out on certain fruit flavors in our national palate. plums and quinces aren't even exotic in this country, but they're hardly used as flavorings. we should try it more.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=syrup-dont-care-p36&gt;syrup: "don't care" (p36)&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;Blackberry juice, 1 quart bottle; grape juice, 1 quart bottle; lemon syrup No. 2, 1 pint; granulated sugar, 4½ pounds.
&lt;p&gt;Dissolve the sugar in the fruit juices at the boiling point, strain, and when cool, add the lemon syrup. Especially good for use in phosphates—8 ounces, 5 cents.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;this was definitely invented by a soda jerk who got sick of making decisions for noncommittal customers. or it's like that restaurant named something like "i don't know, you pick."&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;there's a version of don't care syrup immediately below this one that calls for brandy. it's five o'clock somewhere???&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=egg-milk-thing-arion-p79&gt;egg milk thing: "arion" (p79)&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;Apricot syrup ...... ½ ounce&lt;br/&gt;
Peach syrup ....... ½ ounce&lt;br/&gt;
Rose syrup ........ ½ ounce&lt;br/&gt;
Plain cream ........ 2 ounces&lt;br/&gt;
Egg ............... 1&lt;br/&gt;
Ice ................ ¼ glass
&lt;p&gt;Shake, strain, toss and serve. Price—12 ounces, all milk, 15 cents.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;there are entire genres of drink in this book that barely exist anymore unless you make them yourself. one of these is the egg drink, which i don't think you could persuade most people to try these days. mmm, salmonella. nonetheless, this flavor combo would definitely appeal to &lt;em&gt;me&lt;/em&gt; at the old-timey soda fountain. floral flavors are underrated and i'm glad they're on their way back in.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;isn't it odd that the drink called an 'egg cream' doesn't have an egg? and this one &lt;em&gt;does,&lt;/em&gt; but the name doesn't begin to suggest an egg. bewildering.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=hot-thing-hot-stuff-p93&gt;hot thing: "hot stuff" (p93)&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;Beef extract ....... ½ teaspoonful&lt;br/&gt;
Clam bouillion ..... 1 teaspoonful&lt;br/&gt;
Sweet cream ....... 1 tablespoonful&lt;br/&gt;
Port wine ......... 1 teaspoonful
&lt;p&gt;Place in mug which fill with boiling water. Serve with salt, pepper and celery salt.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;the authors helpfully inform us that hot drinks like this one were invented to bolster foot traffic during the cold months (p89). all this conjures up for me personally is the childhood amalgamemory of drinking beef broth every time i got the flu.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;the name is fun, though. "gimme the hot stuff."&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2 id=milkshake-clam-milk-shake-p72&gt;milkshake: "clam milk shake" (p72)&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;blockquote class="oldtimey"&gt;Clam juice ......... 1½ fluid ounces&lt;br/&gt;
Milk .............. 2 fluid ounces&lt;br/&gt;
Soda water ........ 5 fluid ounces
&lt;p&gt;Add a pinch of salt and a little white pepper to each glass; shake well. Price—8 ounces, 5 cents.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;i learned from this book that ice cream was not always a necessary feature of milkshakes.&lt;sup class="footnote-ref" id="fnref-3"&gt;&lt;a href="#fn-3"&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; the basic chocolate shake recipe in here is just chocolate milk with whipped cream on top. i've always been pretty tepid towards milkshakes as an extension of my tepid feelings towards ice cream. after perusing the ice creamless milkshakes in the book, i realized why i like milk teas from boba shops so much--they're flavored milks with zero ice cream, as god intended.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;i also learned from this book that it is possible to make a milkshake out of anything.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;a chowder is a kind of milkshake, if you think about it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;hr /&gt;
&lt;section class="footnotes"&gt;
&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-1"&gt;&lt;p&gt;while trying to puzzle this out, i found this very cool &lt;a href='https://www.google.com/books/edition/Figures_of_the_Silurian_Fossils/Lo4yAQAAMAAJ'&gt;book of drawings of silurian fossils&lt;/a&gt;, from 1872.&lt;a href="#fnref-1" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-2"&gt;&lt;p&gt;i will never forget when one of my elderly lady professors referred to wallis simpson as a "floozy."&lt;a href="#fnref-2" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li id="fn-3"&gt;&lt;p&gt;according to p27, ice cream was not always obligatory for floats, which used to be ginger ale or grape juice on top of a drink. an "ice cream float" had to be specified.&lt;a href="#fnref-3" class="footnote"&gt;&amp;#8617;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://cherrysroom.bearblog.dev/sodas-of-yore-strange-drinkables-from-new-york-in-1915-new/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-09T07:12:00+00:00</published>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>https://rnotte.art/is-old-stuff-better/</id>
    <title>is old stuff better?</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T19:46:24.013415+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>rnotte</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;this week, i took my 5-year-old iPad pro in to the local tech repair shop to get a new battery, because its original battery was draining too fast for my liking. if i'm going to use it for work, it needs to last.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;which got me wondering, how much are we undervaluing our old stuff?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;between getting this new battery for a 5-year old device that still works wonders, being a regular at thrift stores, and being somewhat of an old tech enthusiast (i'm writing this entry on a genuine windows 7 laptop &lt;strong&gt;;)&lt;/strong&gt;), i've begun to appreciate older items over new ones. we all know that dreaded term: &lt;strong&gt;enshittification:&lt;/strong&gt; the concept of companies making everything worse and worse over the years. our clothes and toys are made with cheaper materials, our devices stop working properly after owning them for 6 months, and new programs are needlessly frustrating to use.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;but then you look at older products. how old are your current computer, phone, and clothes? if they've lasted you 5 years or more, what's the use in buying a new upgrade? (or, &lt;em&gt;"upgrade"&lt;/em&gt;...) if it still works fine, still does its job, and still fits you, then you should keep it for as long as you can. if it breaks, get it repaired. don't buy a new one. seek out copies of previous versions of software you want. and cherish your old items for all their worth. chances are, they were made during a time where companies at least &lt;em&gt;pretended&lt;/em&gt; to give a hoot. at the very least, get new clothes if your old ones don't fit you anymore. and if you want to get something, get it used from a thrift store or ebay. there are so many old items that are languishing in someone's closet or basement, not seeing use even if they're still in good condition. if their original owner won't use them, then &lt;em&gt;you&lt;/em&gt; can.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;so, to answer the question, &lt;strong&gt;is old stuff better?&lt;/strong&gt; i would say, for the most part, yes. at least, better than we perceive it. we should all make an effort to make it part of our lives again.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://rnotte.art/is-old-stuff-better/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-08T19:46:24.013415+00:00</published>
  </entry>

    <id>https://receipts.bearblog.dev/bearblog-has-chosen-me/</id>
    <title>bearblog has chosen me</title>
    <updated>2026-05-07T18:50:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>receipts</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;a couple of hours ago i hit #1 trending on the &lt;a href='https://bearblog.dev/discover/'&gt;bearblog discovery page&lt;/a&gt; for my post, &lt;a href='https://receipts.bearblog.dev/the-freedom-of-writing-anonymously/'&gt;the freedom of writing anonymously&lt;/a&gt;. i hope you understand that this is my equivalent of winning an oscar, and here is my acceptance speech. thank you all for reading! &lt;em&gt;thank you for turning your mind towards my writing.&lt;/em&gt; in that same post i mentioned that it was so much easier for me to write anonymously, but now that a post has actually been seen by quite a few people, it's harder to write because i feel some pressure to improve the quality of my writing so that my future posts can also be received well. (is this how Adele felt?)&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;i've also been surprised by how many different countries bearblog readers are from. i get to see all of them on the analytics page. although most of y'all are from the US, UK or Canada, we also have representation from: Australia, Germany, Brazil, Switzerland, Netherlands, India, Indonesia, Philippines, France, China, Sweden, Singapore, Italy, Belgium, Argentina, New Zealand, Spain, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan, Poland, Romania, Bahrain, South Africa, Malaysia, Norway, Turkey, Ukraine, Latvia, Uganda, Ireland, Bangladesh, Venezuela, Greece and Vietnam. wow!!!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;anyhow, i hope it's clear that this post title is meant to be cheeky and over-the-top. i'll just keep writing for myself mostly, don't want to be breaking down the fourth wall so often (home repairs are costly these days). i do want to start writing reply posts to other bearblog writers though. there are a handful who inspired me to write more candidly online, and i'm immensely grateful for their presence and want to get to know them better. y'all are such a cool bunch of people. this feels like home.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>
    <link href="https://receipts.bearblog.dev/bearblog-has-chosen-me/" rel="alternate"/>
    <published>2026-05-07T18:50:00+00:00</published>

  <entry>
    <id>https://blog.avas.space/social-media-abusive/</id>
    <title>your social media habits sound like an abusive relationship</title>
    <updated>2026-05-09T08:13:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>avas</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Most people in my life still use big social media platforms. My wife, for example, is on Tumblr.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As someone who has been off of these platforms for quite a while, some of the things people share with me sound extremely odd to me; weird rules and behaviors they feel the need to abide by or else!.... Whatever that may be. Some I even recognize from back when I used them, but now I have a completely different view of them as I am no longer embedded in a culture that normalizes them.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;For one, apparently some people are scared of unfollowing others. "&lt;em&gt;I can't unfollow them! We already follow each other for years and they'd notice and then it's awkward!&lt;/em&gt;" so they'd rather stick it out with someone they no longer like or whose posts they don't wanna see. They'd rather filter out all posts via keywords and other means than just unfollow.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Internet strangers! Not even people in real life they'd run into. Why do you feel the need to lie so much just to protect a random person's feelings about having one less follower? The whole concept of being trapped with someone because you're "mutuals" is insane! Why do you care whether only one side follows the other? What does it matter? Why do you fuel the notion that unfollowing means downgrading a friendship or rejecting someone completely? It shouldn't be this way and you voluntarily participate in this.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Same with blocking. "&lt;em&gt;I can't block. That is so harsh. I can instead just block them and unblock them again so we are both unfollowed from each other. This is called softblocking.&lt;/em&gt;" Okay? And what for? So you can pretend it was totally a website glitch that made you guys unfollow each other? As if they wouldn't notice and know. Everyone knows what softblocking is on those platforms! Don't kid yourself.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;When they refollow you again, what then? What if they message you and ask why you unfollowed, the dreadful thing you fear? Many then go on to lie, saying it must have totally been an accident, and follow them again?? Guys, it's a website, pixels on a screen - you &lt;em&gt;can&lt;/em&gt; be honest. They're not gonna stick a hand through your screen to strangle you? Thanks to digital mediums, it has never been easier to just ride out awkward shit and ignore things. Make use of it. Pressing a button is not being aggressive or dramatic.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;"*No, I cannot message them directly, that is awkward, we have never interacted before!" ... so? Damn, the website/app offers DMs and now you can't even privately message strangers on the internet anymore? What has this place come to? Now you're just there to scroll and passively consume ads and no longer talk to the people that share the ads around voluntarily? DMing someone is "intimate"? You are "harassing" someone with a simple message they can choose to open or ignore? Do you hear yourself?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Then there is the far more subtle or platform-specific stuff... like the fact that people feel like they can't comment in the replies until others have done so, or cannot reblog something because the post is still "too small"; that liking old posts is "creepy"; watching or not watching a story, liking or not liking a post has deep consequences; you have to put things in the tags instead of the post body to be safe of OPs wrath and signal that this is for your followers only (just for OP to screenshot the tags anyway and rake you over the coals).&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There's also people that are too scared to challenge others directly and openly on the respective post, and instead screenshot it, put a water filter over it to visually signify they disagree with its content, and then post it themselves? The type of stuff they are comfortable to say when they think OP won't notice, while being too scared to do it underneath the post, and just living off of follower validation like "&lt;em&gt;Look how dumb this is! Hype me up, like this post, comment that you agree!&lt;/em&gt;" is so embarrassing to see.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As people on there are treating public interactions as definitive signs and ownership, when someone bad follows &lt;em&gt;you&lt;/em&gt; and likes your posts, while you don't even follow back, you're still treated as attracting and tolerating the bad person, therefore implicitly agreeing to their vile views. I guess that's where the whole culture of "&lt;em&gt;Do Not Interact&lt;/em&gt;" disclaimers comes from, because you have to prove from the get-go where your alliances are and as a precaution for when you haven't deeply vetted every follower you have. In the same vein, people seem to proactively confess old opinions, archive tweets, lock accounts, or add disclaimers to avoid or soften hypothetical future attacks.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It all adds up to weird stories... I can't even completely recall it, investigative, roundabout stuff with second accounts and softblocking and other checks, weaponizing features of the platform, circumventing things, completely normalized mutual surveillance disguised as casual browsing, where they manually actively check who viewed stories, who liked posts, posting times, and other activity to judge the friendship level?&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;All of this is tip-toeing around, scared to offend someone, worried about nebulous consequences and being subject to toxic rage; never getting out of the awful behaviors you're subjected to by your peers in high school. It's as if you're in an abusive relationship with the platform and its users, and it's uncomfortable to see from the outside how scared it makes you to actually interact with anyone online or use the space for what it is made for. It's like your online home constantly has signs of a punch hole in drywall.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I see it with my wife as well, who also has a blog on here and sometimes would like to reply to some other blog posts on Bearblog, but never ends up doing it because "&lt;em&gt;It's weird to barely post and then immediately shit on someone else's post.&lt;/em&gt;" and other convoluted reasons that only exist because social media culture is what it is.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If you relate to anything in this post, you have been conditioned by people who can only scream and shout and "&lt;em&gt;I am not reading all that&lt;/em&gt;" and siccing their followers on you. How sad! You're like a beaten puppy and your behaviors are completely warped.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It's actively harmful for you, and I wouldn't be surprised if it significantly fuels the social anxiety you feel even when offline. In the online spaces you're in, you are always asked to put the needs of someone else above yours that you cannot even fully anticipate because they're a nebulous mob entity. Your nervous system constantly deals with the risk of using this app or site blowing up in your face, and you're always scared when you see a bunch of notifications coming up. I don't know how you can feel mentally well when this is always looming over your head.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Spending my online time in places where none of this weird stuff exists has really put it into perspective. I can just reply! I can just send emails or reach out otherwise! No stress, no worries! No followers, no blocking!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Again, I know why all these exist in theory, and many I've known from my own time on these platforms, but none of it is justified - period. You don't have to tell me why any of these are valid or why they happen; this is like listening to an abuse victim justify the abuse. Sometimes you can only see how badly you've been treated months or years after you leave.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='mailto:avas.space@pm.me'&gt;Reply via email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br /&gt;

    09 May, 2026
&lt;/time&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>https://blog.lauramichet.com/check-out-amberspire/</id>
    <title>Check out Amberspire!</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T04:39:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>lauram</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Nic Tringali, &lt;a href='https://blog.enceledean.com/'&gt;whose blog&lt;/a&gt; I've linked to many times here in the past, just released a new videogame!!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href='https://store.steampowered.com/app/3350750/Amberspire/'&gt;Amberspire&lt;/a&gt; is a very tense, quite difficult citybuilder where resources are generated by dice rolls. Each building can roll its own die to generate a bunch of unusual &lt;em&gt;stuff&lt;/em&gt; that other buildings then consume. But each die has a chance of triggering negative things, too... most crucially "weather dice," which can damage your city at the end of each round. The game requires you to make very judicious decisions about which buildings to generate resources with, where to build, and what to &lt;em&gt;give up&lt;/em&gt; on as you go.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;I feel very bad at this game, so far! But I still feel like I'm getting better at it, and I still feel like I'm learning something. I've played about ten hours of it!&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Anyway, if this sounds like the kind of thing you'd enjoy, you should check it out!!&lt;/p&gt;
</content>

  <entry>
    <id>https://blog.absurdpirate.com/scams-that-we-just-accept/</id>
    <title>Scams That We Just Accept</title>
    <updated>2026-05-08T14:05:00+00:00</updated>
    <author>
      <name>absurdpirate</name>
      <email>hidden</email>
    </author>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;America is a racket and it's corruption only gets more noticeable with each day. I kinda wanted to talk about some stuff that is so blatantly a scam, but it's so integrated into our society we have kinda no choice.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Insurance:&lt;/strong&gt; Imagine if you will, paying $50-$200 per month for the off chance that something will happen and when something does happen, the thing you've been paying money to protect you for denies protecting you. That's basically American insurance. It doesn't matter if you're talking car or health. It all sucks. They basically collect money to do fuck all with it when it comes time to actually needing it. Health insurance is basically a control tool by employers to make sure you're too piss scared to quit or demand better treatment.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;College:&lt;/strong&gt; I don't say this like some get rich guru that tries to belittle continuing education. Those guys would find Gen Ed difficult. I'm talking the entire tuition system. Thousands of dollars you have to spend every semester, and for the first 2 years it's the same bullshit classes you took in high school. God help you if you have to retake a class or change your major. Maybe it wouldn't be so bad if degrees meant shit anymore, but good lord even then the price is nauseating. And don't even get me started on the cost of college textbooks. You'll spend $100 on a fucking PDF file that you'll use maybe a handful of times.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cars:&lt;/strong&gt; Car ownership is fucking RIGGED. Car dealerships want you stuck in this infinite loan loop so bad that they'll actually prefer someone who takes a loan vs. someone who pays in cash these days. Not to mention, if you have anything older than like a 2008, your repair cost is going up because mechanics can't fucking fix these damn things. Either because they were designed by a some asshat who looked at a bowl of pasta and thought it was perfect engineering, or that they don't have the diagnostic system to actually fix any computer problems in your car. Gas fluctuates more than a menopausal woman having hot flashes. All this so that you could have the freedom to get stuck in 7am rush hour traffic. It wouldn't be so terrible if we had sensible public transit in this gods-forsaken country, but because our politicians are cheaper than a can of Pepsi, they're all bought and paid for by automotive lobbyists. Henry Ford can burn in hell. If you're going to get a car, get an older model Honda or Camry and learn to do basic maintenance. Oil changes from mechanic, $80. Oil change from myself and it takes maybe 10 minutes, $30.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Warranties:&lt;/strong&gt; You'll often always get asked to buy some dipshit protection plan whenever you buy some electronic or anything worth more than a few hundred dollars. They're pointless. They're usually only for up to a year, and that's usually before things actually start going wrong with your device. If you pay attention, warranties tend to expire before typical hardware failure. Yeah if you constantly shake like a constipated Chihuahua and drop your phone constantly, maybe get one. But for most people, it's cheaper and more practical to just buy a hard case... or just take care of your crap.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Free Shipping:&lt;/strong&gt; It's not free shipping. Shipping is never free unless what you're buying from has their own shipping service like Amazon (but even then there's backend costs). The shipping is always factored into the cost of the item if it's not explicitly stated. If you're buying an item that's $15 + free shipping, there's a good chance that Item is like $12.50 + $2.50 shipping. It's all marketing.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Online subscriptions:&lt;/strong&gt; It's not fucking 1998 anymore, why the hell are gaming companies still charging for you to play online? That was a rhetorical question, we all know why, doesn't make it any less stupid. Look, the Netflix of games costing money is fine, but Jesus why am I needing to pay money for something literally every modern device does for fucking free? It's why PC ownership is much cheaper in the long run, yeah there's a greater up-front cost, but the cost of subscriptions to online services, the lowered functionality, the lack of mod support, so on and so forth just make consoles look gimped in comparison. I kinda miss when consoles costed like $300, it actually made sense to own a console over a PC back then. I bought my first computer back in 2013, guess what? All the games I bought back then I can play on my entirely new rig and they look better than ever! I could go on a whole rant of why PC gaming is the best, but I'll save that for my gaming blog. Back to me bitching about other stuff.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Online Skins:&lt;/strong&gt; BaCk WhEn I wAs A bOy... If you told a gamer in the 2000s people were paying $10 for essentially horse armor, they'd look at you like that fish from Spongebob after Spongebob put only one ice cube in his drink. Seriously, I was looking at discord, $5 for a fucking border over your profile picture... that shit should be $0.99 TOPS.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Phone plans:&lt;/strong&gt; The whole system encourages infinite debt loops similar to that of car manufacturers. They want you paying year after year. Paid off your phone? Guess what you can upgrade! Oh but we're gonna charge you $60 to press a button and swap out your SIM card. Fucking What? Don't you cunts get enough money from my cell plan? People will buy mid-upper tier cell plans and only ever really use the unlimited calling/texting from the bottom tier.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Maybe you've got some other things you've notice to just be a complete racket. This is kinda the things I notice that impact me the most.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a class="previous-post" href="/to-smartphone-or-not-to-smartphone" title="To Smartphone or Not to Smartphone"&gt;Previous&lt;/a&gt; | &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3 id=as-of-writing-this&gt;as of writing this...&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;My folks are coming into town for mother's day. It's gonna be nice spending time with them. I woke up late today since it's Friday and nobody is in office early. So I can walk in late and leave early and nobody is there to tell me I can't. In-office policies can suck a fart out of my ass.&lt;/p&gt;

    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;"When I’m on my phone, I don’t have to think. I’m just scrolling, and afterward, I can’t remember what I saw. When I didn’t have my phone, I couldn’t stop my thoughts. They were overflowing." —— Salome Slouk, 16&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;"At home, I noticed that my mom, my brother, my dad, all of them, were on the phone all the time, and I was the only one in the house without a phone. I was really annoyed. I often told them not to do that, but they didn’t listen to me." —— Özlem Koza, 11&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;These quotes were from &lt;a href='https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/world/europe/smartphones-austria-children-experiment.html?unlocked_article_code=1.g1A.8cwU.7TDVX-UuXw99&amp;smid=url-share' target='_blank'&gt;this NYT piece&lt;/a&gt; about Austrian tweens and teens who ook part in a three-week "voluntary digital detox." It's an interesting piece and I think you should read it.&lt;/p&gt;
